rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Garden of Refuge is beside the Lote Tree.
rows.anchor: Cennetü’l-Me’vâ onun yanında yani sidrenin yanında.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is the destination of the God-fearing, or of the spirits of martyrs.
rows.anchor: müttakīlerin veya şühedâ ervâhının varacakları cennet.

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Enes
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's account that the Sidra changed into a beauty no one could describe when covered by God's command.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Enes radıyallâhu anh demiştir ki: “Resûlullah buyurdu: ‘Melek beni Mi‘râc’a çıkardı

rows.speaker: İbn Zeyd
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Zayd says the Prophet saw golden moths cover the Sidra, with an angel glorifying God on every leaf.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr’de İbn Zeyd’den: “Yâ Resûlallah, Sidre’yi gaşyeden ne gördün?” denildi, buyurdu ki: فـَرَاشٌ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that God covered the Sidra and Muhammad saw the greatest of his Lord's signs.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan: إِذْ يَغْشَى ٱلسِّدْرَةَ مَا يَغْشَىٰ “onu Allah gaşy etti de Muhammed Rabbinin âyâtından en büyüğünü gördü.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covering here should be understood as an act or attribute of action.
rows.anchor: Bu gaşy sıfat-ı fi‘l olmak gerektir.

rows.speaker: Rebî‘
rows.claim: Rabī‘ says the Lord's light and the angels covered the Sidra.
rows.anchor: Rebî‘’den: “Sidre’yi Rabbin nûru gaşy etti ve melâike gaşy etti.”

rows.speaker: Ebu’l-Âliye
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliyah says the Creator's light and angels covered it, like birds gathering on a tree.
rows.anchor: Ebu’l-Âliye’den: “Onu Hallâk’ın nûru gaşy etti ve melâike gaşy etti

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: Mujahid says Muhammad saw the Sidra and saw his Lord with his heart.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid’den: “Muhammed, Sidre’yi gördü ve Muhammed kalbi ile Rabbini gördü.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's gaze did not stray or glance askance despite the astonishing sights; this expresses his proper adab.
rows.anchor: Göz şaşmadı onu gören Resûlullah’ın gözü kaymadı, şaşıp da sağa sola bir eğri bakmadı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His sight did not exceed its proper limit or see falsely; this expresses its strength and precise observation.
rows.anchor: وَمَا طَغَىٰ} ve aşmadı görmek haddini tecavüz edip de yanlış bir görüş de görmedi.

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi contrasts Muhammad's steadiness with Moses fainting when the mountain was leveled; the Sidra stood firm and Muhammad was not shaken.
rows.anchor: Râzî der ki: “Mûsâ aleyhisselâm’a olduğu gibi olmadı, zira onda cebel düpedüz olmuş

none: This segment contains only the verse translation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists imagined idols as angels and angels as God's daughters, hoping images of them would bring closeness and intercession; the passage refutes this by affirming God's sovereignty.
rows.anchor: Müşrikler putları melâike suretleri ve melâikeyi Allah’ın kızları farzederek onların suretlerini yapıp takmakla

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels cannot intercede on their own; without God's permission their intercession is useless, and any intercession remains subject to Him.
rows.anchor: şefaatleri hiçbir şeye yaramaz izinsiz şefaat etmek hadleri değildir a, ettikleri farzedilse yine fâide vermez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission and approval condition may restrict both the angels who intercede and the people for whom they intercede.
rows.anchor: bu hem şefaat edeceklere hem de şefaat olunacaklara kayd olabilir.

words: إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعْدِ أَن يَأْذَنَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God alone permits and approves intercession, He, not angels or idols, is the deity whose pleasure must be sought.
rows.anchor: Demek ki önünde sonunda rızâsı aranacak olan mâbud melekler değil, Allah’tır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because they do not truly fear afterlife accountability, its deniers call angels female and claim they are God's daughters.
rows.anchor: Evet, muhakkak ki âhirete imanı olmayanlar günahın ve Allah’a karşı yalan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They make idols in female form to suit their desires and call the angels God's daughters.
rows.anchor: melâikeye dişi adı verip duruyorlar “Allah’ın kızları” diyorlar. Onun için nefislerinin hevâsına uyacak vechile kız suretinde putlarını yapıp duruyorlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have no knowledge of what angels are or what they say; their claim is not based on knowledge.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh ona dair bir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here zan means imagining or conjecture: they suppose female representations would be more attractive.
rows.anchor: buralarda “zan” tevehhüm mânasınadır. Yani dişi tasavvur ve tasvir olunursa daha câzibeli olacağını zannediyorlar.

words: وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّنَّ لَا يُغْنِى مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ شَيْـًۭٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conjecture cannot replace truth; doctrinal matters requiring certain faith cannot rest on mere speculation.
rows.anchor: Onun için yakīn ile iman lâzım

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to turn away from those who reject the reminder, namely the Qur'an that recalls truth, conveys it, and admonishes them.
rows.anchor: Bizim zikrimizden, yani hakkı ihtar ve tebliğ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those seeking only worldly life include Nadr ibn al-Harith and Walid ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: dünyâ hayattan başka bir şey istememekte Nadr b. Hâris, Velîd b. Muğire gibi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their knowledge reaches only the worldly life and its pleasures, as also stated in 30:7.
rows.anchor: O onların ilimden erebildikleri gaye varabildikleri son had, yani bildikleri o kadar, bütün ilimlerinin nihâyet murâdı dünyâ hayat zevkidir.

words: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows best those who persist in straying and those who accept guidance; this explains the command to turn away, and repeating that He knows best marks the contrast between them.
rows.anchor: Bu cümle i‘râz emrini ta‘lîldir, هُوَ أَعْلَمُ kavlinin tekrârı da her iki mâlum arasındaki tebâyünü ilandır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge here is knowledge that orders and implements the corresponding punishment or reward.
rows.anchor: “İlim”den murad da ikāb ve sevâbını tertib ve tatbik edecek vechile ilimdir.

words: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in heaven and earth belongs to God by creation and by ownership.
rows.anchor: Hem Allah’ındır bütün göklerdeki ve yerdeki halkan da O’nun, milken de O’nundur.

rows.speaker: Kādî Beyzâvî
rows.claim: Baydawi reads the lām causally, attached to the preceding implication: God created and ordered the world for this purpose, or distinguished and preserved the states of the straying and guided.
rows.anchor: Kādî Beyzâvî der ki: “Mâkablinin medlûlüne illettir, yani âlemi şunun için halk ve tesviye etti

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the lām may attach to the meaning of God's ownership, or to the phrases about those who stray and are guided.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyân milk mânasının medlûlüne أَيْ يُضِ ُّل وَيـَهْدِي لِيَجْزِيَ. وَقِيلَ: بِقَوْلِهِ: بِمَنْ ضَ َّل، وَبِمَنِ اهْتَدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reports Razi's view that attachment to the turn-away command is possible but attachment to knowledge is closer; Abu al-Su'ud prefers the latter.
rows.anchor: Ebussuud da bunu tercih eylemiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes such lām clauses in divine acts to express wisdom and outcome: the purpose is to recompense evil and good deeds.
rows.anchor: ef‘âl-i ilâhiyede bu gibi lâm’lar hikmet ve âkıbet içindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God repays wrongdoers in keeping with their bad deeds and rewards those who do good with what is better: Paradise or multiplied recompense.
rows.anchor: kötü iş yapanları yaptıklarıyla cezâlandıracak kötü amellerine mukabil misli olan kötü cezâ verecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Major sins are sins carrying a grave punishment or specifically threatened in revelation.
rows.anchor: ikābı büyük olan, yahut hakkında bihusûsihi va‘îd bulunan günahlar kebâirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fawahish are especially the manifestly shameful acts among major sins.
rows.anchor: kebâir meyânında bilhassa çirkinliği açık olan fuhşiyyâttan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lemam means small faults; when major sins are avoided, lesser lapses such as a glance, insinuating look, or kiss are forgiven.
rows.anchor: Çünkü kebâirden ictinab edilince meselâ bir nazar, bir gamze, bir bûse gibi sağāir ma‘füv olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forgives minor sins when major sins are avoided, may forgive major sins upon repentance or even without it, but does not forgive shirk without repentance.
rows.anchor: kebâirden ictinab edilince sağāiri mağfiret buyurduğu gibi tevbe edilince kebâiri de mağfiret buyurur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows people completely, from the first human or human cell created from earth, or the earthly origin of their food, through their embryonic state and future conditions.
rows.anchor: Arz’da ilk insan cinsinin, insan huceyresinin yaratılışı zımnında veya insan gıdasının topraktan yaratıldığı sırada

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People must not praise themselves as entirely pure and faultless, since they may have many faults of which they are unaware.
rows.anchor: hiç günahsız, kusursuz, tertemiz addederek övmeyin,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone fully knows who is truly pious; the people of good and evil will be distinguished before Him in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: Ehl-i ihsan ile ehl-i isâe âhirette huzûr-ı Hak’ta seçileceklerdir.

rows.speaker: Mücâhid ve İbn Zeyd
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd report that Walid ibn al-Mughira listened to the Prophet and neared Islam, but a polytheist promised to bear his afterlife burden for payment; Walid turned back, paid a little, then stopped.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid’den ve İbn Zeyd’den rivayet olunduğu üzere Velîd b. Muğīre Resûlullah’ın meclisine gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ikda means reaching hard, unexcavatable rock while digging; by extension it means withholding or refusing to give.
rows.anchor: “Küdye” kazılmaz katı yer ve yalçın kaya, “ikdâ” da küdyeye varmak mânasınadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question challenges whether he can see the unseen and thus knows that someone else will carry his afterlife burden.
rows.anchor: Şimdiden âhireti görüyor da günahını başkasının yüklenivereceğini biliyor mu?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scrolls of Moses refer to the Torah.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ’nın suhufundaki ile yani Tevrat ile

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham fulfilled all the words with which he was commanded and tried, remaining faithful to his commitments in every matter; 2:124 is cited.
rows.anchor: mantûkunca me’mur ve mübtelâ olduğu kelimâtı tamamıyla îfâ etmişti.

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan reports a view that before Abraham people were held liable for relatives' or masters' crimes; Abraham first rejected this, and from his law to Moses's law people were not charged with another's crime.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyân Bahr’da şöyle der: “Mûsâ ile İbrâhim, bu iki peygamberin tahsîsi için denilmiştir ki: Nûh ile İbrâhim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The central intent is to state the afterlife rule that no soul bears another's burden.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh asıl murad hükm-i uhrevîyi beyandır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle an is lightened, with the pronoun of شأن omitted, so the construction means wa-annahu.
rows.anchor: ki doğrusu bu اَن muhaffefedir, zamîr-i şan mahzuf olup

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Vizr means sin and a heavy burden; here it means sin and bearing its punishment, so no one pays another's afterlife penalty.
rows.anchor: günah ve ağır yük mânasına gelir ki burada günah ve günahın cezâsını çekmek mânasınadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The legal maxim is that punishment cannot be delegated: each person bears their own offense, and cannot rescue another by taking that person's sin.
rows.anchor: Bunun ta‘bîr-i fıkhîsi “ukūbâtta niyâbet câri olmaz” kā‘ide-i külliyesidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who undertakes another's burden instead incurs their own added burden, as stated in 29:13.
rows.anchor: belki kendi taahhüdünün cezâsını çeker وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقَالَهُمْ وَأَثْقَالًۭا مَّعَ أَثْقَالِهِمْ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith says whoever establishes a bad practice bears its burden and the burden of those who act on it until Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: مَنْ سَ َّن سُن َّةً سَي ِّئَةً فـَعَلَيْهِ وِزْرُهَا وَوِزْرُ مَنْ عَمِلَ بِهَا إلَى يـَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ

words: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person is not entitled as their own to reward from another's striving, just as they are not liable for another's crime; another's gift may still be donated to them.
rows.anchor: Yani bir insan başkasının cürmü ile muâhaze olunmayacağı gibi kendi sa‘yinden başkasıyla sevablanmak da kendinin has hakkı değildir.

words: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rule is aligned with 2:286, which assigns each soul what it earns and against it what it acquires.
rows.anchor: لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse cannot mean that people receive nothing beyond their own effort, since divine gifts and mercy reach them, and cooperation is commanded and beneficial.
rows.anchor: insana gerek dünyada olsun gerek âhirette sa‘y ü kesbinden başka vehbî olarak verilen nice rahmet ve atâyâ-yı ilâhiye bulunduğunda da şüphe yoktur.

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: Benefits from prophets' intercession, angels' prayers for forgiveness, and the living's prayers or charity for the dead rest on the recipient's own faith and righteousness; without faith they do not benefit.
rows.anchor: Ebussuud der ki: “Enbiyânın şefaati, melâikenin istiğfârı, dirilerin ölüler için duası, sadakası gibi

rows.speaker: Hüseyin b. Fazl
rows.claim: Asked by Abdullah ibn Tahir about 2:261 and this verse, Husayn ibn Fadl replied that justice gives only what one strove for, while grace gives as much as God wills; the governor kissed his head.
rows.anchor: Hüseyin ona “adl ile ancak mâ-se‘â, fazl ile ise Allah’ın dilediği kadar vardır” diye cevap verdi

words: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is consistent with 52:21, which says every person is held for what they earned.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Tûr’a bak كُلُّ ٱمْرِئٍۭ بِمَا كَسَبَ رَهِينٌۭ

words: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: The report that Ibn Abbas called this verse abrogated is not sound; the majority holds the verse definitive and unabrogated.
rows.anchor: Bunun mensuh olduğuna dair İbn Abbas’tan söylenen söz sahih değildir.

rows.speaker: İbn Atıyye
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the lām is the pivot: only one's own striving is truly one's due; intercession, righteous relatives' care, multiplied good deeds, and pure grace are mercy, not one's property or entitlement, except metaphorically.
rows.anchor: İbn Atıyye bunu şöyle tahkik eder: “Bence bu âyette tahrir şöyledir: Mânanın mihveri لِلْإِنسَٰنِ’daki lâmdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām indicates اختصاص or entitlement, and the restriction focuses on that relation; ma is primarily a verbal noun meaning striving, though it may be relative, since not everything a person strives for becomes theirs.
rows.anchor: “Mâ-se‘â”daki مَا masdariyyedir, sa‘y demektir, sa‘y ettiği mânasına mevsûle olması ihtimâli de melhuz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person's striving will be seen in the record and placed on the scales at the Resurrection; its fruit is not necessarily immediate, but the effort is not lost.
rows.anchor: kıyamet günü defterinde görülecek ve mîzânına konulacaktır. Yani sa‘yi boşa gitmez, fakat onun semeresini peşin ve fi’l-hâl görmeye kalkışmamalıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afterward the person receives the fullest recompense, so one's future is the product of one's striving.
rows.anchor: Sonra ona en dolgun karşılık verilecektir. Bu suretle insanın istikbâli sa‘yinin mâhasali olacak demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone ultimately returns to God and is gathered before Him, where complete recompense is realized; He is the First and the Last.
rows.anchor: Bütün halk sonunda dönüp O’na varır, O’nun huzûruna haşr u ihzar olunur, işte o vakit o tam cezâ da hakka’l-yakīn olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laughter and weeping are opposing manifestations of life: joy and pain, reminders of reward and punishment, Paradise and Hell, and divine beauty and majesty.
rows.anchor: hayâtın tecelliyâtından iki mütekābil hâlet ki biri neş’e nişânesi biri elem, biri muhtıra-i sevab biri muhtıra-i ikābdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone causes death and gives life.
rows.anchor: Ve hakikat öldüren ve dirilten de O’dur başkası değil.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates male and female pairs among humans and animals from a drop when it is emitted into the womb; only He creates such variety and opposites.
rows.anchor: Gerek insanlardan ve gerek hayvanlardan erkek ve dişi bütün çiftleri O halketmektedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God undertakes the afterlife resurrection and will deliver reward and punishment; paired creation in this world points to an afterlife.
rows.anchor: Ölümden sonraki âhiret neş’etini de O taahhüd eylemiştir; O yapacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that God enriches the poor and supplies capital, freeing them from need; it may also mean that He makes them content, as in 93:8.
rows.anchor: fakir olan bir kulunu ihtiyaçtan kurtarıp sermayedâr eden, yahut hoşnut eyleyen
